reason: The base revision still matches unsupported Y tokens and lets them fall through to the timezone-offset fallback, so the lone Y and YYY outputs do not match the expected literals.
The revised format regex recognizes only YY and YYYY, so unsupported lone Y and YYY tokens remain literal as required.
The change only centralizes the existing percent-decoding check and preserves decoding of route parameters.
The new shared helper still decodes percent-encoded route parameters, while the refactor removes only duplicated logic.
Before the fix, reschedule updates Redis but leaves the same SortedEntry's in-memory score and time stale, so the direct handle check fails.
The applied change assigns the new timestamp to @score after rescheduling, so score and at on the existing handle reflect it.
The pull request changes Range-header parsing only and does not affect Content-Type parsing or charset parameters.
The change is limited to whitespace handling in Range parsing and leaves Content-Type parsing behavior unchanged.
The pull request changes repository download error messages only, not Composer archive creation or zip timestamp preservation.
The logging-only change does not alter package archiving, so repeated archives retain the existing timestamp behavior described by the test.
The pull request concerns CredentialCache URI prefix comparison and is unrelated to JSON deserialization of nullable parent properties.
The CredentialCache path-comparison change does not affect synchronous or asynchronous JSON deserialization.
The cursor FETCH FIRST fix is unrelated to INET operators and quantified subquery execution.
The cursor fix does not modify INET containment operators, array handling, or ANY expression parsing.
Before the change, an IPv6 NO_PROXY entry is treated as a wildcard domain and can produce an invalid URL pattern, causing client construction to fail.
The applied code detects IPv6 addresses and creates a bracketed bypass pattern, avoiding the construction error for ::1.
The base implementation rejects regex flags such as DOTALL during Series.str.match validation, so the newline match request fails.
The revision explicitly preserves support for DOTALL both through flags and through a compiled pattern, yielding the expected match results.
Before the fix, preparing a chain with a group in the middle can lose recursive result-parent state, so reconstruction does not preserve all four group children.
The fix updates the previous task and result after processing the middle group, preserving the recursive parent structure through serialization and reconstruction.
The reported bug concerns -- as the first argument, whereas this case supplies values before --, so the existing parser behavior satisfies the expected handoff.
The applied terminator-precedence change preserves the first positional's values and hands --check to the trailing positional without an error.
Before the patch, a late OSC11 response uses the ordinary option setter, which triggers OptionSet and the resulting background change triggers the expected events.
The applied code deliberately uses noautocmd when setting background, suppressing OptionSet, so the test's requirement that both autocommands fire is not met.
The pull request only changes compile-time handling of Inspect derives and does not affect required-field changeset validation.
Reordering the conditional read of @derive does not change required-field validation, so the omitted field still produces the expected blank error.
